_note: Every request this phone builds, as one shared fixture for two test suites.
The Kotlin half (AgentdRequestWireTest) asserts that `Agentd`'s builders
produce exactly these, so a builder that changes shape is caught. The Rust
half (apex-agent-core/tests/android_requests_wire.rs) deserializes each one
into `apex_agent_core::protocol::Request` and asserts the variant, so a
request the phone sends that the daemon cannot parse is caught too.
That second half is the guard this unit needed and did not have. Two
separate rounds of work were built on the claim that `worktrees` was not a
verb — a claim read off `request.rs`'s privileged-operation `Verb` instead
of off `protocol.rs`'s wire `Request`. A fixture the daemon's own serde
must accept cannot be wrong about which verbs exist: a verb that is not
there fails to deserialize, and a verb that is there and spelled wrong
fails too.
`decide` is deliberately absent and must stay absent. privilege.rs:1176
refuses it from any non-local origin before the pending check, so a phone
can neither approve nor deny, and a builder for it would be a builder for a
request that is always refused. See Approvals.kt.
`input` appears ONCE, and that is the point. A typed reply, a push-to-talk
transcript and a clipboard send all reach the wire through the SAME
builder, because they all reach it through Reply.bytes and Reply.check.
Voice and clipboard put text in the reply box for a person to read; Send
is what terminates it. A second, un-terminated send path would be a second
place for the recycled-session-id guard to be forgotten, and forgetting it
types somebody's sentence into a stranger's terminal. See Handoff.kt.
There is NO file-upload verb and no clipboard verb, and neither is an
oversight to be fixed by adding one here: a Frame::Control carries at most
MAX_PAYLOAD = 65514 bytes, so a single-frame handoff tops out near 48 KB of
base64 and a screenshot is 100 KB to 2 MB. Chunked transfer is a protocol
unit. See Handoff.Files.
